clue.text: Upright member of the Royal Mail

parts.note: king: the head of a royal house
post is another word for mail

explanation.surface: A loyal postal worker at the Royal Mail who stands up straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright member' sounds like a respectable employee, but it is a builder's term: a king post is the central vertical beam in a roof truss.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry this is a vertical beam running from a roof's tie-beam to its apex.

clue.text: Peacock's tail is found to be musical

indicators.note: tail picks out the final letter of the word Peacock's

parts.note: taken as written
met, as in came across, means found

explanation.surface: A peacock's tail feathers turn out to have a musical quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' looks like an adjective about the tail; it is a noun, the stage musical of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a Broadway stage show of 1953, so it is a musical.

clue.text: Irritation is eliminated in the shade

indicators.note: eliminated tells us the word is is removed from the longer word

parts.note: an irritation is a nuisance
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting out of the sun removes an irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eliminated' takes IS out of NUISANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle gradation of colour or meaning is a shade.

clue.text: Screw-fitting includes an old measure…

indicators.note: includes means one word holds the measure inside it

parts.note: proper means fitting or appropriate
an ell is an old unit of cloth length

explanation.surface: A screw fitting containing an old measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw-fitting' reads as one hardware term; split it: 'Screw' is the definition (a ship's screw) and 'fitting' gives PROPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's propulsion device with rotating blades is called its screw.

clue.text: … one tended to be fixed

parts.note: single means one
minded means looked after or tended

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: one person was inclined to be stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses join this to 3 Down as one sentence, but each clue is solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with one purpose is fixed or determined on it.

clue.text: Swimmer's first stroke with bad hand

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word Swimmer's

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A swimmer's opening stroke is let down by a poor hand position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' in a swimming context suggests the hand in the water; here it means handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand means handwriting, and untidy, hurried handwriting is called a scrawl.

clue.text: Shock, supporting Conservative seat

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts the piece beneath the other

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair

explanation.surface: A political jolt as a Tory loses or wins a parliamentary seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' means a shock of hair; 'supporting' in a down clue puts HAIR under C.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of furniture to sit on is a seat.

clue.text: Measure of Swedish physicist's concern, capital being short

parts.note: angst is anxiety or concern

indicators.note: being short means the city name loses its final letter

parts.note: Rome is a capital city

explanation.surface: A Swedish physicist worried about a capital running short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being short' trims ROME to ROM.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of length of a ten-billionth of a metre is named after the Swedish physicist Anders Ångström.

clue.text: Put down a large number in India, may be

parts.note: to land is to put down, as of an aircraft
a mass is a large number of people or things

explanation.surface: Crowds being set down in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes last: India is an example of a large continuous area of land (a subcontinent).
explanation.definitionFit: A subcontinent such as India is an example of a large continuous expanse of land.

clue.text: The main condition of course for putting out?

parts.note: the main is an old poetic name for the open ocean
in horse racing the going is the state of the ground on the course

explanation.surface: A question about the state of a golf course before putting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' and 'course' suggest golf; the definition means putting out to sea, so a vessel built for the open water.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship described this way is fit for voyages on the open ocean, i.e. for setting out from port.

clue.text: Jabberwock's beginning with gas and gibberish

indicators.note: beginning asks for the opening letter of the word Jabberwock's

parts.note: argon is a noble gas

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky starts with hot air and nonsense words.
explanation.definitionFit: Unintelligible technical language is dismissed as gibberish, a synonym.

clue.text: Laura, girl cut out for such duties in land army

definitions.text: for such duties in land army

indicators.note: out signals the letters of Laura, girl cut are put out of order

explanation.surface: Laura was a young woman cut out for farm work in the wartime Land Army.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Land Army was a British wartime organisation of women doing farm work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Land Army did farming work, so its duties were of the farming kind.

clue.text: Compere at full stretch?

definitions.meaning: a compere is the host who introduces acts at a show
the two letters MC written out in full, stretched into a word

explanation.definitionFit: A host of a show is an MC, and spelling those letters out as a word gives the same person.

clue.text: Oral might upset this exponent of arithmetic

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of oral might are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker's forceful delivery might disturb a mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exponent' looks like a person who champions something; mathematically it is a power, which is exactly what this value is.
explanation.definitionFit: This value is the power to which a base must be raised to give a number, i.e. an exponent.

clue.text: Holding the lead to pub four miles out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of pub four miles are put out of order

explanation.surface: A runner leading a race heading to a pub four miles away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lead' is the metal (Latin plumbum), not first place in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral containing the metal Pb is described with this word, from Latin plumbum.

clue.text: Dish left in broken-down hacienda

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation within the rearranged letters
broken-down tells us hacienda is to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something was left behind in a dilapidated Mexican ranch house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken-down' rearranges HACIENDA, and 'in' places L within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled tortilla with a filling and chilli sauce is a Mexican dish.

clue.text: Powerful shot, struck with tremendous success

parts.note: a smash is a hard overhead shot in tennis
hit means struck

explanation.surface: A powerful shot strikes the ball and wins hugely.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely popular song, show or film is called a tremendous success.

clue.text: A gnome admits society can be testing

indicators.note: admits means letting another piece inside

parts.note: a gnome can mean a pithy saying or maxim

explanation.surface: A garden gnome lets in a society that is trying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' is not the garden ornament but the rare word for an aphorism; 'admits' puts S inside A SAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysing metal to find its purity is testing it.

clue.text: Incorrectly judge motorway's stress?

parts.note: mis- is a prefix meaning wrongly
to pronounce is to declare a judgement

explanation.surface: Someone misjudges the pressures of driving on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: putting the stress on the wrong syllable of a word such as 'motorway' is saying it wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressing a word on the wrong syllable is saying it wrongly, a specific case of the verb.

clue.text: Outcome of a lob?

definitions.meaning: a lob is a shot hit high up into the air

explanation.definitionFit: The final result of events is their outcome; read literally, a ball hit high is an upward shot.

clue.text: More reticent sort who shuts up

definitions.meaning: more tight-lipped and secretive, comparative of an adjective
a person who shuts something, such as a shop at night

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative means more secretive; a person who closes things is literally one who shuts.

clue.text: But does the bank-teller produce it?

definitions.text: But does the bank-teller produce it?

parts.words: But does the bank-teller produce it?
parts.note: a teller is someone who tells or states things, so a teller ought to produce a declaration; but the bank's printed account summary comes by post, not from the cashier

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bank cashier hands over a printed account summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank sends customers a periodic account summary, and a teller in the sense of one who tells makes a declaration.

clue.text: Need mast-head repair in port?

indicators.note: repair means the letters are put back together in a different order
head picks out the first letter of the word mast

explanation.surface: A ship's mast top needs fixing while in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes M from 'mast' and 'repair' rearranges it with NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Emden is a port city in north-west Germany.

clue.text: Urge to drive

definitions.meaning: to urge is to press forward
to drive is to force onward

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean pushing someone or something forward into action.

clue.text: Locks function with a bang, for example

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair
a do is a party or function

explanation.surface: A party with locks and explosions.
explanation.walkthrough: A bang (American usage) is a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead, not an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe cut straight across, called bangs in the US, is one style of haircut.

clue.text: Opens most of the best fish inside

indicators.note: inside says the fish goes within the trimmed word
most of means the word best loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler unveils the finest catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the word for best to its first three letters, and 'inside' puts the fish within that; 'Opens' is a verb, as in opening a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a topic or a cask is to broach it; 'opens' and the answer are both third-person verbs.

clue.text: Nurse clutches silver remnant

indicators.note: clutches means holding the other piece tightly inside

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A nurse clings to the last of the family silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap or end piece of something is a remnant.

clue.text: For such a bloomer, look back to spring holiday

indicators.note: back means the word for look is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
Easter is a holiday in spring

explanation.surface: Looking back fondly on a spring break.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bloomer' here is a flowering plant, not a blunder: the oleaster is a flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster, or wild olive, is a shrub that produces flowers, so it is a plant that blooms.
